# Starter: course puller delete semantics

## Setup

```
npm install
npm test          # runs the test suite once
npm run test:watch
npm run type-check
```

You should see all 4 tests in `test/reconcile.test.ts` **fail**. That's the
starting state, not a setup problem.

## The task

`src/reconcile.ts` exports `reconcileCourses`, a function that's supposed to
reconcile a local "courses" store against a fetch from an external system:
upsert every fetched row, delete rows that no longer belong. It's a
simplified stand-in for a real periodic sync job. Right now the function
body is just `throw new Error("not implemented")` — a stub. The JSDoc
comment above it is the contract: read it carefully before you write
anything, it's the actual spec you're implementing against.

Two things the contract requires that are easy to get wrong:

1. **Delete semantics.** The store keeps one row per
   `(courseId, subject, number)` — a single course can have multiple rows
   across its renumbering history, and past-term data still joins against a
   courseId long after that specific number is no longer current. You must
   not delete a row just because its `courseId` doesn't appear anywhere in
   the fetch — a courseId can be legitimately, permanently absent from
   every fetch (e.g. discontinued upstream) while still being referenced
   elsewhere. Deletion needs a more specific signal than "courseId missing."

2. **Fetch completeness.** The fetch is paginated internally, and
   `fetchCourses()` reports which (simulated) pages failed via
   `failedPages`. A fetch with any failed pages is not a trustworthy full
   snapshot — reconciling against it anyway can delete data that's still
   valid upstream, purely because of a transient page failure. Your
   implementation must refuse to write anything in that case.

Implement `reconcileCourses` to satisfy both requirements, drawing on your
Round 1 design(s) for delete semantics and fetch completeness (feel free to
revise that design now that you're looking at the concrete types). Your
implementation is done when `test/reconcile.test.ts` passes: normal
reconciliation, a renumbering scenario, a still-referenced discontinued
course, and a partial-fetch scenario. All four should pass when you're done.
Don't change the tests or the fixtures in `src/fixtures.ts` to make them
pass — if a test seems wrong, say so in your notes instead of editing around
it.

You're free to shape `src/reconcile.ts` however you like (helper functions,
different control flow, etc.) as long as the exported `reconcileCourses`
signature in `src/types.ts` still holds and the tests pass without
modification.
